title: Secondary sex ratio among women exposed to diethylstilbestrol in utero.
ehr_evidence: Data were provided by women participating in the National Cancer Institute (NCI) DES Combined Cohort Study.
summary: Cohort study evaluating the association between in utero diethylstilbestrol (DES) exposure and the secondary sex ratio of offspring among US women.
key_findings: Overall, no significant association was observed between in utero DES exposure and secondary sex ratio (adjusted OR 1.05, 95% CI 0.95–1.17).

Among women with complete dose and timing data (33%), those first exposed earlier in gestation (<13 weeks) and to higher cumulative doses (≥5 g) had a significantly higher odds of a male birth (adjusted OR 1.24, 95% CI 1.04–1.48).
Results did not vary appreciably by maternal age, parity, cohort, or infertility history.
captured_features: gestational timing of first DES exposure
data_source_type: Research cohort / Questionnaires and medical records
population: Parous US women (daughters of DES-exposed mothers) from four NCI cohorts
limitations: High proportion of missing data on DES dose and timing (67%)
Reliance on self-reported reproductive and medical history
Potential for residual confounding despite adjustment
Small sample sizes in some cohort subgroup analyses
